summary: The paper presents a preregistered white-box audit of a repository-defined evidence contract for autonomous MLIP research. Across a finite catalog of 48 single-fault traces and four clean controls, semantic re-derivation covered all declared faults while a mutable manifest-hash ablation covered four. A separately attested two-iteration MACE replay illustrates why a metric pass is not sufficient for promotion when a frozen reproducibility constraint fails. All released claims are infrastructure-only.
strengths: The question, fault catalog, seeds, budgets, endpoint, thresholds, fallback, and claim ceiling were frozen before the new experiment.
Every headline value is recomputed from an immutable 52-row ledger and bound to hashes; negative MACE decisions are retained.
The paper clearly separates T1 local infrastructure facts, T2 remote infrastructure observations, and excluded scientific claims.
The anonymous evidence packet resolves public claims without exposing exact repository commits or local paths.

Independent review caused two explicit post-execution amendments: a macro-aggregation representation correction and disclosure that the timing endpoint was under-specified. Neither case execution nor the primary decision was changed.
weaknesses: The fault suite and grader share the same white-box repository contract, so the result is finite contract coverage rather than independent robustness evidence.
The mutable manifest-only comparator is intentionally weak and is an ablation, not a competitive provenance system.
The four seeds are deterministic trace instantiations with identical pass/fail patterns, not independent statistical replications.
Only four clean traces were tested, so specificity is reported as an observed 0/4 count without population inference.
The real-MACE case contains two one-step iterations on one L4, no frozen-test release, no physical-property validation, and a binary exact-equality rerun flag.
The preregistered wall_seconds endpoint lacked a per-method timing boundary and is excluded from interpretation.
questions_for_authors: How well would the grader cover faults authored independently or held out from contract development?
How would performance change against an append-only, consumer-owned, or externally anchored provenance baseline?
Can exact equality be replaced by tolerance-aware deltas calibrated to decision stability across devices and software versions?

ethics_and_limitations.known_harms: The main risk is overinterpreting a self-authored finite fault suite as general scientific validity; the title, abstract, limitations, claim audit, and excluded-claims list explicitly prohibit that inference.

release_conditions: Keep the claim ceiling at T2 and scientific_status at infrastructure_only.
Do not describe the fault result as adversarial robustness or the MACE percentages as scientific improvement.
Preserve both amendment records, the external weak-reject assessment, and all negative MACE decisions.
